FLOCK HEALTH

A stronger foundation for poultry health.

Product choices work best within a complete flock programme: biosecurity, nutrition, housing, observation and veterinary assessment all have a role.

IN THIS GUIDE

All resources
01

Protect the flock boundary

Manage the movement of people, equipment and animals into poultry areas. Use clear hygiene procedures, maintain cleaning and disinfection routines, and take steps to reduce contact with wild birds and pests. Biosecurity is a repeated daily practice rather than a single intervention.

02

Notice meaningful changes early

Changes in water or feed intake, activity, mortality or production can help identify a developing problem. Keep comparable records and discuss unusual patterns with the flock veterinarian. Reliable observations support diagnosis and avoid treating every performance change as the same disease.

03

Review the complete ration

Vitamin A supports epithelial tissues. Vitamin D₃ contributes to calcium and phosphorus metabolism, relevant to skeletal development and eggshell quality. Vitamin E and selenium have complementary roles in antioxidant protection. Review the complete diet, feed preparation and storage before adding supplements; both deficient and excessive intake matter.

04

Connect products to a veterinary plan

Nutritional support and anti-infective treatment have different purposes. Confirm the exact product and formulation, its authorised species and any route or withdrawal requirements. Use product documentation together with veterinary advice, and record the response of the flock.
